title: Marguerite and the Thorn
premise: Wren Winterbourne has spent ten years hiding in Thornvale, a valley where magic dies at the border, posing as an ordinary scribe while his storm-calling gift lies dormant. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley hunting the last storm-callers, Wren flees with Marguerite, a sharp-tongued cartographer who turns out to be hunting him for the bounty. Together they discover that the 'ancient war' the crown fears was actually a massacre of storm-callers by the first king, and the secret Wren carries — the location of the surviving storm-caller enclave — could either save his people or doom them. In the end, Wren chooses truth over loyalty to his hidden enclave, revealing its location to Marguerite and the court, forcing a reckoning that spares the enclave but costs Wren his magic forever.
about_author: T. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval storm charms before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse on the coast, where they claim the weather always agrees with them.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ten years after crossing into Thornvale, Wren lives quietly as a scribe until a royal proclamation arrives: all bearers of the gift must surrender for 'protection.' The valley's dampening effect on magic has kept him safe, but the proclamation names storm-callers specifically. Emotional beat: dread settling into a life built on forgetting.

chapters.title: A Cartographer's Errand
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She arrives in Thornvale claiming to map the valley's uncharted caves, but her true commission from the crown is to find the exiled storm-caller rumored to live there. She notices Wren's ink-stained hands and the way birds go silent around him. Emotional beat: predatory patience disguised as friendliness.

chapters.title: What the Border Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Witch-hunters arrive ahead of Marguerite's report, dragging a half-dead boy who carries a sealed letter from the storm-caller enclave — addressed to Wren by his birth name. The letter warns that the enclave's location has been discovered. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Thornline
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren flees Thornvale with the wounded boy, and Marguerite pursues — but when hunters corner them at the border, she makes a split-second choice and kills a hunter instead of Wren. Crossing the line, Wren's dormant magic stirs like a waking animal. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged in blood.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Traveling together toward the enclave, Marguerite grapples with guilt and growing affection as Wren tends the boy and shares stories of the family he lost. She hides her commission deeper with each mile. Emotional beat: found family taking root where loyalty should have died.

chapters.title: The Enclave of Nine Storms
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They reach the hidden enclave, where Wren learns the truth: the 'ancient war' was the first king's genocide of storm-callers, erased from every record. The enclave elders order Marguerite's execution as a crown spy. Emotional beat: homecoming poisoned by old wounds.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Imprisoned in the enclave, Marguerite bargains with the elders using her maps and knowledge of the crown's hunt — but Wren must choose between defending her and obeying the people who raised him. He testifies that she saved his life. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined as truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Hunt Comes Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The crown's army finds the enclave anyway, guided by Marguerite's earlier reports. In the battle, Wren unleashes his full storm-calling power for the first time, and the wounded boy is killed shielding him. Emotional beat: rage and grief fusing into terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Secret Given Away
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the capital, Wren stands before the young queen and reveals everything: the massacre, the erased history, the enclave's location — betting that truth will do what hiding never could. Marguerite corroborates with her maps and testimony. Emotional beat: the climax of trust, everything staked on honesty.

chapters.title: Where the Rain Lands
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The queen pardons the enclave but binds Wren's magic as the price of peace; he returns to Thornvale powerless but free, with Marguerite choosing exile beside him. The valley's rain falls ordinary now, and he no longer needs it to be anything else. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — memory honored, family chosen.
